segments.text: diff - compare files line by line
Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.
report when two files are the same
output NUM (default 3) lines of copied context
output NUM (default 3) lines of unified context
output at most NUM (default 130) print columns
output only the left column of common lines
show which C function each change is in
show the most recent line matching RE
use LABEL instead of file name and timestamp (can be repeated)
expand tabs to spaces in output
make tabs line up by prepending a tab
tab stops every NUM (default 8) print columns
suppress space or tab before empty output lines
pass output through 'pr' to paginate it
treat absent first files as empty
ignore case when comparing file names
consider case when comparing file names
exclude files that match any pattern in FILE
start with FILE when comparing directories
compare FILE1 to all operands; FILE1 can be a directory
compare all operands to FILE2; FILE2 can be a directory
ignore case differences in file contents
ignore changes due to tab expansion
ignore white space at line end
ignore changes in the amount of white space
ignore changes where lines are all blank
ignore changes where all lines match RE
strip trailing carriage return on input
output merged file with '#ifdef NAME' diffs
format GTYPE input groups with GFMT
format all input lines with LFMT
format LTYPE input lines with LFMT
These format options provide fine-grained control over the output
lines common to FILE1 and FILE2
LETTERs are as follows for new group, lower case for old group:
if A equals B then T else E
contents of line, excluding any trailing newline
printf-style spec for input line number
Both GFMT and LFMT may contain:
the character with octal code OOO
the character C (other characters represent themselves)
try hard to find a smaller set of changes
keep NUM lines of the common prefix and suffix
assume large files and many scattered small changes
color output; WHEN is 'never', 'always', or 'auto'; plain [[p0]] means [[p1]]'auto'
the colors to use when [[p0]] is active; PALETTE is a colon-separated list of terminfo capabilities

FILES are 'FILE1 FILE2' or 'DIR1 DIR2' or 'DIR FILE' or 'FILE DIR'. If [[p0]] or [[p1]] is given, there are no restrictions on FILE(s). If a FILE is '-', read standard input. Exit status is 0 if inputs are the same, 1 if different, 2 if trouble.
